name: Beth Orton
label: Partisan
lede: She began on a Japan-only record, became the voice on two Chemical Brothers tracks, and got stuck with folktronica as a word. Then she bought a £300 piano in Camden Market and made the best-reviewed album of her career.

eras.title: Dereham, Dalston and a record almost nobody heard
eras.text: Before any albums there was a stage-school kid from Norfolk, a long detour, and a William Orbit session that only ever came out in Japan. The club world found her voice before the record shops did.

years.h: Elizabeth Orton is born in Dereham, Norfolk
years.p: She moves to Dalston, East London, at fourteen and ends up at the Anna Scher Theatre School, acting before she sings.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia she did her A-levels at City College Norwich and toured experimental theatre productions in the UK, Russia and Ukraine before music took over.

years.h: Her mother dies of cancer; she leaves for Thailand
years.p: Orton is 19. Wikipedia says she lived for a time with Buddhist nuns.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes her mother as a journalist and political activist.

years.h: Burn Blind: a William Orbit record released only in Japan
years.p: Credited to Spill and made with [[William Orbit|a7412cd0-e0b8-4fa1-8d24-75bb92a84946]], it came out in a tiny run (Wikipedia estimates 1,000 to 5,000 copies).
years.xp: Wikipedia says the songs were co-written with Orbit, apart from a John Martyn cover, and that some were recycled: "She Cries Your Name" resurfaced on Trailer Park, and another track became "Montok Point" on Orbit's Strange Cargo Hinterland (1995).

years.h: A one-word vocal, then a co-write, with Red Snapper
years.p: [[Red Snapper|89abed31-3a93-407e-a4a3-a94e193488cd]] put her on their first EP and on "In Deep" from The Swank EP. Their bassist Ali Friend later joins her live band.

years.src: Irish Examiner: The entire room went mental · Wikipedia: Beth Orton
years.h: "Alive Alone" puts her on the [[The Chemical Brothers|1946a82a-f927-40c2-8235-38d64f50d043]]' first album
years.p: Exit Planet Dust gives her a voice on dancefloors before she has a solo record out.
years.xp: Orton told the Irish Examiner she first heard it at the Heavenly Social, the club night at the Albany pub in central London, where the Chemical Brothers played to about sixty people.

eras.title: Trailer Park and the Mercury years
eras.text: Heavenly signs a folk singer who sounds like she was mixed in a club, and the UK takes to it. Two Mercury nominations and a Brit in four years.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trailer Park (album) · Irish Examiner: The entire room went mental
years.h: Trailer Park: acoustic songs, breakbeats, [[Andrew Weatherall|4f4fd405-6ede-4da0-9b74-c422d8e09bed]]
years.p: Produced by Weatherall and Victor Van Vugt for Heavenly. It earned two Brit nominations and a Mercury nomination; Pitchfork later gave it 8.0.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits Orton with co-writing everything except a cover of "I Wish I Never Saw the Sunshine", and says William Orbit co-wrote "She Cries Your Name". It peaked at No. 68 in the UK and is certified Platinum there (300,000 units).

Decades later she told the Irish Examiner of Weatherall, who died in 2020: "We made good music together."

years.h: "She Cries Your Name" is re-released and cracks the UK Top 40
years.p: Her first Top 40 hit arrives months after the album it opens.

years.h: Best Bit EP: a Fred Neil cover with [[Terry Callier|44fd61e1-119c-479e-8301-8ac5c77148bf]]
years.p: Their version of "Dolphins" reaches No. 38 in the UK. She spends the summer on Lilith Fair.

years.src: Irish Examiner: The entire room went mental
years.h: "Where Do I Begin" on the Chemical Brothers' Dig Your Own Hole
years.p: The Irish Examiner calls it the 1990s clubland answer to the Beatles' "A Day in the Life". She sings on Come with Us (2002) too.

years.h: Central Reservation, with "Stolen Car" as the single
years.p: Recorded across six studios with producers including [[Ben Watt|9030ae90-4db2-4a9c-aa08-01cf17a86b58]], [[Dr. Robert|8a494ebb-ed3b-43bb-bb91-e563bf2b490a]] and [[David Roback|10886c9d-c106-4337-9653-430989ec484e]]. Terry Callier and [[Ben Harper|1582a5b8-538e-45e7-9ae4-4099439a0e79]] guest.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia it reached No. 17 in the UK and No. 110 on the Billboard 200, went Gold in the UK, and earned a second Mercury nomination. "Stolen Car" peaked at No. 34 and the title track at No. 37 on the UK singles chart.

years.h: Brit Award for best British female
years.p: She wins at the 2000 Brits after nominations in 1998.

eras.title: Bigger rooms, then the lights down
eras.text: Daybreaker takes her to the UK top 10 and the US Billboard chart, then she strips everything back and records an album in two weeks with Jim O'Rourke.

years.h: Daybreaker: Ryan Adams on guitar, the Chemical Brothers in the mix
years.p: It reaches No. 8 in the UK and No. 40 in the US. Pitchfork gave it 4.8; Mojo called it her best to date.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Orton, Victor Van Vugt and Ben Watt as producers, with [[Ryan Adams|c80f38a6-9980-485d-997c-5c1a9cbd0d64]] playing on multiple tracks; it also notes Emmylou Harris and Four Tet among the collaborators. Metacritic's score was 70. It was recorded at Ridge Farm Studio in Surrey and Eastcote Studios.

Q was blunter than Pitchfork's number suggests: it found "a crippling shortage of choruses".

years.h: She ends the Daybreaker world tour at the Royal Albert Hall
years.p: The double compilation Pass in Time follows in 2003 with B-sides, rarities and Orbit and Chemical Brothers material.

years.h: Comfort of Strangers: two weeks, [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]], no electronics
years.p: Recorded in spring 2005 at Sear Sound in New York with O'Rourke on bass, piano and marimba. Pitchfork gave it 7.2.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Orton played guitar, piano and harmonica, with Tim Barnes on drums. The record peaked at No. 24 in the UK and No. 92 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Her daughter Nancy is born
years.p: Orton had cancelled a September 2006 UK tour because of the pregnancy.

eras.title: Bert Jansch, Portland and a synth record
eras.text: A long quiet, a new label and a husband who plays on the record. She comes back acoustic, then swerves into keyboards.

years.h: Open tunings from [[Bert Jansch|d7f95537-2b48-403d-9ac2-f1fc7aad0960]]
years.p: Wikipedia says she learned the open guitar tunings that shape her later acoustic work from the Pentangle guitarist. Her touring guitarist Ted Barnes and bassist Ali Friend had left to form Clayhill.

years.h: Her son Arthur is born
years.p: She and [[Sam Amidon|2e088ea8-b8f7-4df4-ac83-7024a50aabf1]] had married; the family lives in Los Angeles until 2015, then returns to London.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sugaring Season · Wikipedia: Beth Orton
years.h: Sugaring Season: first album in six years, first for ANTI-
years.p: Produced by [[Tucker Martine|3faa4491-806c-4e7f-a6a5-a9e41135d088]] at his Flora studio in Portland, Oregon, with Amidon playing on it. Pitchfork gave it 7.7.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Brian Blade on drums, Rob Burger on keys and Marc Ribot on guitar. It reached No. 26 in the UK and No. 90 on the Billboard 200; Metacritic scored it 76.

years.h: Kidsticks: she hands the keyboards to herself
years.p: Co-produced with Andrew Hung of [[Fuck Buttons|f4640b20-b76b-40d3-9ffc-a38b6718b273]], with Chris Taylor of Grizzly Bear and Twin Shadow's George Lewis Jr. Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
years.xp: The Guardian called it a real reinvention. Wikipedia lists the release date as 27 May 2016 and the Kidsticks album page as 25 May, so the page says May.

years.h: The "1973" video: spray paint on a Joshua tree
years.p: A Change.org petition followed and the video was taken down; Orton apologised and the Mojave Desert Trust welcomed it.
years.xp: Wikipedia cites Billboard and Stereogum on the removal and says the Mojave Desert Trust responded positively to her outreach.

eras.title: A shed, a piano and a saxophone
eras.text: She goes quiet again for six years, deals with chronic illness, loses Andrew Weatherall, and builds an album around a used piano.

years.h: A lost Chemical Brothers collaboration surfaces
years.p: A cover of Tim Buckley's "I Never Asked to Be Your Mountain" is released after turning up, Wikipedia says, inside an unread copy of War and Peace.

years.h: The Guardian: "I was losing words"
years.p: Orton talked about Crohn's disease and drug complications affecting her voice and memory.
years.xp: Wikipedia cites the interview and quotes her: "I was losing words. I didn't remember the week before."

q: You would play one note and about 10 would come out.
years.src: American Songwriter: Beth Orton Finds New Magic · Uncut: Beth Orton
years.h: She buys a used piano in Camden for £300 and trades in an old one
years.p: She writes the album's songs on it and records in her own London studio.
years.xp: American Songwriter says the piano came from Camden Piano Rescue and that the dealer, Desmond O'Keeffe, shipped her old Berry piano to Africa for children there. Uncut says she began in a garden shed with simple modal patterns, homemade MIDI soundscapes, and Alice Coltrane and Talk Talk as touchstones.

years.src: Album of the Year: Weather Alive · Wikipedia: Weather Alive · The Quietus: Beth Orton Details New Album · Uncut: Beth Orton
years.h: Weather Alive: Pitchfork gives it 8.7 and ranks it No. 23 of 2022
years.p: Eight songs, self-produced, with Tom Skinner, Tom Herbert, Shahzad Ismaily and Alabaster dePlume. Pitchfork's Sam Sodomsky called it the best work of her career.
years.xp:
Album of the Year lists Pitchfork's score as 87/100 and its year-end placement at No. 23; the same page has The New York Times ranking it No. 3 and Spectrum Culture No. 1. Metacritic had it at 85 on twelve reviews, and it peaked at No. 27 in the UK. Uncut gave it 8/10.

It was her first album for Partisan, after ANTI- and Decca. Craig Silvey mixed it and Greg Calbi mastered it.

years.src: The Quietus: Beth Orton Details New Album · The Vinyl Factory: Beth Orton weaves
years.h: Tom Skinner plays on it while drumming for [[The Smile|9055fca5-69bc-4d47-b569-ab2012a19565]] and [[Sons of Kemet|fee950a2-e68c-4e76-b1ae-ff6efdf68b11]]
years.p: The Quietus and The Vinyl Factory both list him, Tom Herbert of [[The Invisible|08d43582-cee9-42a0-8ec7-bbf8389f62c2]], Ismaily and dePlume as the band.

eras.title: Judging books, making part two
eras.text: She turns up at the Booker Prize panel, then returns to the studio for a second self-produced record.

years.src: Irish Examiner: The entire room went mental
years.h: She sits on the International Booker Prize judging panel
years.p: The Irish Examiner also has her looking back on the Heavenly Social years with clear eyes.

years.src: The Line of Best Fit: Beth Orton announces
years.h: The Ground Above arrives on Partisan
years.p: Self-produced again, with Shahzad Ismaily, Tom Herbert, Dave Okumu and others, mostly captured live in the room.
years.xp: The Line of Best Fit says lead single "Waiting" draws on Laura Nyro, Carole King and Terry Callier, and lists eight UK headline dates from 12 October in Brighton to Alexandra Palace Theatre on 22 October.
